## TL;DR

Implemented the post-upgrade restart experience for task #1075. The server now compares its startup version with the installed version on disk, exposes restart status and active-work counts, and supports immediate or idle restart requests through the supervisor. The dashboard presents the pending restart notice, and the CLI reminder and restart command cover terminal workflows. The requested scoped check passed after the remote runner retried on a second host.

## Work and rationale

The implementation extends the release/update status path rather than adding a competing update endpoint. That keeps the installed-version notice beside the existing release reminder and reuses its client polling and dismissal behavior. The server records the version it started with, reads installed version metadata locally with caching, and returns running and installed versions, whether a restart is pending, counts of active agents and checks, supervisor status, and idle-restart state.

Restart behavior is routed through the existing managed-service lifecycle. A supervised server schedules a clean process exit so systemd or launchd can bring it back. An unsupervised server returns a clear refusal with the manual restart command; the UI disables restart actions in that case and displays the command. The idle option stays pending until agents, reviewers, and checks are no longer active, and can be cancelled. The CLI restart command uses the same server action, while upgrade checks for a running server and prints a version-specific reminder when appropriate.

The dashboard notice names both versions, reports current work counts, warns about interruption and links to issue #0214, and provides Restart now, Restart when idle, and dismiss actions. A pending state replaces the restart choices with a waiting message and cancel action. The component refreshes status and reconnects after the process restart. Light and dark preview fixtures were added for review.

The change includes route parity registration, unit and UI coverage for version comparison, supervisor detection, restart scheduling, and upgrade messaging, plus the updating guide and release dialog copy. No new configuration key was needed.

## Approaches tried

I first ran the reported pressure-guard case in isolation under strict timing mode. It passed locally, and inspection showed that the test feeds a deterministic fake probe into the wait loop; there was no local reproduction or code change associated with the reported failure. I therefore kept that unrelated production code unchanged and relied on the scoped remote suite to check whether the failure repeated.

The first remote validation host (ThinkPad) stopped responding and RepoOS marked the run hung, removed that validation container, and retried on Bee. The retry rebuilt the project, ran all changed-path tests, then ran UI smoke and rendered contrast checks. The retry passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The only validation obstacle was the first remote host hanging after bundle upload. RepoOS recovered by retrying on a second host; no code workaround was needed. The check reported 377 test files passing, with 5,381 tests passing and one skipped. The rendered contrast audit passed in both check phases, UI smoke passed, and the user-docs build completed.

The code has not been exercised against a real systemd or launchd installation during this run. Restart behavior is covered with injected/fake supervisor and process-exit seams, so production service behavior still depends on the platform service manager honoring its restart policy.

## Key learnings

The reported pressure-guard failure was not reproducible in the scoped worktree: its focused test passed locally, and it did not recur in the full changed-path remote run. The first remote stall was a validation-host issue, not a test failure; the automatic retry provided a clean result.

The restart notice belongs in the existing update-status flow because users encounter it as the next stage of the release reminder. Keeping version detection local and cached makes the feature independent of network availability, while the explicit unsupervised path avoids suggesting a restart action that could strand a manually launched server.
